transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The U.S. and Israel are preparing for a possible attack on Iran in early November after the
midterm elections.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reports that's according to a person briefed on the matter.
The person briefed on the U.S. and Israel's war planning spoke to NPR on condition of
anonymity to discuss the preparations.
The person said Israel had initially planned to strike Iran in mid-October about two weeks
before Israeli elections October 27, but President Trump objected.
The person briefed said the U.S. is now amassing forces in the region to be ready for an attack
by early November, after U.S. midterms November 3, but that these preparations could also
be part of a campaign to pressure Iran to reach a diplomatic deal.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is campaigning for reelection on a threat to
topple Iran's regime.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
President Trump is urging Ohio Republican candidate for governor Vivek Ramaswamy to
keep running a controversial ad featuring the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent,
Amy Acton.
It comes after bipartisan criticism of the ad, including from outgoing Ohio Republican
governor Mike DeWine.
It was wrong to run this ad, and even at this late time, my wife friend saw the ad run this
morning on TV, I would just urge the Ramaswamy campaign to take this down.
Acton's mother lost custody of her after Acton's stepfather was indicted for raping her when
she was 12.
In the ad, Acton's mother calls her a liar.
DeWine, whose term limited, said he still supports Ramaswamy's bid for governor.
Trump called DeWine "disloyal" and that the ad was "hitting pay dirt."
The Department of Justice has begun notifying places it wants to monitor on Election Day,
and Pierre's Miles Parks reports.
Adams County, Colorado was one of the first counties in the country to get a monitoring
notification.
The county clerk there, Josh Zigglebaum, a Democrat, told NPR he likes to assume the
best in people, but he's worried the decision to pick his county may have been for political
reasons, based on the way President Trump talks about voting.
The rhetoric has really pointed the country in a direction of mistrust towards election
offices, and I'm concerned that some of the motivations behind this is to perpetuate that.
The DOJ says this year's monitoring effort will be the largest in the department's history.
And the department says it will prioritize areas with a history of voter access issues
and places with competitive races.
Miles Parks, NPR News, Washington.
A federal judge has ordered President Trump to sit for a deposition in his defamation
lawsuit against the BBC by December 11th or face sanctions, including possible dismissal
of the lawsuit.
The BBC's lawyers say Trump has repeatedly delayed his appearance.
Trump is seeking $10 billion in damages over a BBC documentary.
The latest shutter for AI stocks pulled markets lower today around the world.
The majority of U.S. stocks actually rose.
This is NPR News.
The International Criminal Court has won the European Union's top human rights honor,
the Sakharov Prize.
The award comes just days after the Trump administration announced sweeping new sanctions
on the ICC.
The sanctions are part of a campaign to dismantle the tribunal over investigations into certain
conduct by the United States and its allies, including Israel.
Here's a new heavyweight pumpkin champion, NPR's Ava Pukach spoke with the man who grew
the world's first ever 3,000-pound pumpkin.
Rhode Island gardener Ron Wallace has grown giant pumpkins for more than 30 years.
His prize winner weighed in at 3,156 pounds.
So how do you squash the competition?
Wallace says the key is genetics.
This hobby is very scientific and soil biology and using different growth hormones for cell
division and cell elongation, which will help the pumpkin grow to get to maximum size.
Wallace says he'll harvest the seeds from the pumpkin and donate them to growers' clubs
across the country.
And then a team will attempt to turn the world's largest pumpkin into the world's largest
jack-o'-lantern.
Ava Pukach, NPR News.
Scientists say Vincent van Gogh's The Starry Night may have been inspired by gazing up
from his French asylum 137 years ago.
A South Korean team reports it has matched his masterpiece to a pre-dawn sky from around
July 22, 1889.
That's a month later than the long-accepted time frame for the painting.
Results were published in scientific reports.
I'm Rylan Barton.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: US and Israel prepare possible Iran attack in early November, after midterm elections
Trump urges Ramaswamy to pull ad featuring estranged mother of Amy Acton
DOJ notifies counties it will monitor polling places on Election Day, including Adams County, Colorado
Judge orders Trump to sit for deposition by December 11 in $10 billion BBC lawsuit
AI stock selloff pulls global markets lower, though most U.S. stocks rise
International Criminal Court wins European Union's Sakharov Prize amid U.S. sanctions
Rhode Island gardener Ron Wallace grows world's first 3,000-pound pumpkin
Scientists link Van Gogh's Starry Night to a pre-dawn sky from July 22, 1889
